By \texttt{def:target}, the causal estimand is
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
             -\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \texttt{ass:consistency}, \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely, so equality of the conditional expectations appearing in \texttt{def:target} gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\tag{2}
\]
By \texttt{ass:event-date-transport},
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (2)--(3) into the finite sum (1) yields
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is derived from, rather than used to define, the causal contrast.  No regression, modulus, or sampling condition enters this equality.

Let \(A\) and \(D_X\) be as in (1) of \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  We first prove the upper bound in the deterministic experiment.  For \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\), condition under \(\mathbb Q_\xi\) on the donor sample, let \(t_{s\ell}\) be the selected nearest indices, and define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The mean restrictions in \texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment} make (1) conditionally centered.  Its product restriction makes the \(U_{si}\) independent across \((s,i)\).  Since the fold coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one and all outcomes lie in \([-B,B]\), \(|U_{si}|\le4B\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_iU_{si}\mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)\right)
 \le16B^2A.
\tag{2}
\]

Nearest-neighbor optimality and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(0<\lambda\le1\), subadditivity and Holder continuity imply
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda
 +\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda
 +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive.  Balanced folds have \(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and the donor mean and covariance restrictions yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\tag{5}
\]
The local parameter restriction similarly gives \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Jensen's inequality applied to (5), followed by (2)--(4), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 \le CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}},
\tag{6}
\]
where the last step is (11) of \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.

We now prove the converse under \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  We use the following elementary two-law inequality.  If laws \(P_0,P_1\) have targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), separation \(\Delta=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), then, for every estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), the event \(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\) gives
\[
 \max_v\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.
\tag{7}
\]

For the treated-mean channel, fix the other coordinates of the experiment and, under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent \(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\) with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,\qquad
 \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\tag{8}
\]
For a sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\), all probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The targets are separated by \(4\gamma\sqrt A\), and the Hellinger affinity is at least
\[
 \prod_s(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-8\gamma^2/b^2).
\tag{9}
\]
Thus (7) gives risk at least \(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel, use the functions \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) from (6) of the geometry lemma.  They agree at every design site.  Choose identical response, donor, and event laws under the two alternatives.  The observed laws are identical, while their targets differ by \(aD_X\); (7) gives risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel, translate and linearly transform the three-point construction (1)--(6) in \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} so that its covariance is the displayed full \(\Sigma\) and its first standardized direction points into the trimmed cube at the given \(z_0\).  Strict interior and moment slack make this possible for a displacement \(c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Use the same affine surface when \(\lambda=1\), or the same one-sided \(\lambda\)-cusp when \(0<\lambda<1\), under both alternatives.  The response and event laws are identical, the donor total variation is bounded by \(1-\eta_0\), and the targets differ by \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (7) gives risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the largest of the three lower bounds and using (11) of the geometry lemma proves the two-sided comparison.

For a causal law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the conditional-mean equalities, cross-unit independence, donor separation, donor moments, and bounded support imply that its observed regular conditional kernel, together with its induced labels, defines an element of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(P\)-almost every \(X\).  By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, its experiment target equals \(\tau(z_0)\).  This proves the asserted causal upper bound without assigning a conditional law at a null design.

If every cohort has an exact site at \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and (11) gives the exact-site reduction.  Finally suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\).  Then \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is admissible in every fold's anchor search, and selected-certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
The bandwidth floor gives \((Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Local-constant convexity, Holder continuity, (5), and (10), combined with the variance argument (1)--(2), yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,X]
 \le CR_D
\tag{11}
\]
for \(P\)-almost every such \(X\).  The geometry lemma gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).  Neither (10) nor (11) supplies a converse in terms of the Gram certificate.

Put
\[
 A=\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},\qquad
 D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\tag{1}
\]
On the event where the attained anchor comparison is available, \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives the conditional risk bound \(CR_D\).  On its complement, clipping and bounded wealth bound squared error by \(16B^2\).  Averaging over the exact design and using both conclusions of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The fallback contribution \(CT^{-2}\) is absorbed by \(D_T\).  No lower local-modulus condition was used.

The smoothing expression in (2) is redundant.  With \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\),
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{3}
\]
Therefore, since \(S\) is fixed,
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{4}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  After translating both support points into a fixed subinterval of \((0,B)\), the treated-sign construction (8)--(9) in the conditional proof embeds into the base causal class by using independent uniform designs, a common admissible donor law, consistency, and event-date transport.  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\), the horizon-zero return equal to the desired positive wealth minus one, and all later returns zero verifies \texttt{def:buyhold-level}; (7) then yields the lower bound \(cA\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Fixing any auxiliary error probability in \((0,1/2)\), lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two laws with a common subprobability measure of positive mass and target separation \(cD_T^{1/2}\); applying (7) gives \(cD_T\).  Taking the largest of these three subexperiments and using (4) proves the reverse inequality in (2).

On the independent-calendar subclass, the no-log conclusion of the anchor-moment lemma gives the upper spacing term \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For its converse, choose a ball of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\) and two Holder regressions that agree outside the ball and differ at its center by \(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  The density upper bound gives probability at most \(C_Xv_dr_T^d\) for one design point to hit the ball, so for sufficiently small fixed \(c\),
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the ball for every }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.
\tag{5}
\]
On this event the observed regression experiments coincide while their targets differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Inequality (7) from the conditional proof gives the lower bound \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).  Substitution of \(S=1\), \(d=1\), and \(n_1=n\) gives the scalar display, and (4) proves the claimed domination.

Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} first identifies the causal target with the observed-law functional.  On the regular branch, condition on the exact design and donors.  Replacing the nearest-site weights in (1) of the conditional proof by the actual selected local-constant weights gives one centered bounded contrast for each \((s,i)\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} centers these contrasts; donor--training separation and cross-unit independence make them independent across \((s,i)\).  For every random variable \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}
 \le\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Exponential Markov applied with the actual absolute weight sums therefore yields
\[
 \Pr\{\text{unitwise stochastic error}>r_{\mathrm{unit}}\mid z_0,X,Z\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2.
\tag{2}
\]
The displayed linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is a bounded-range correction, so no estimated variance is inverted.

For the calendar construction, the cross-fit in \texttt{def:honest-interval} excludes each retained score block from the weights used for that block.  Replace the retained blocks successively by independent copies within the two parity collections.  Absolute regularity bounds the total replacement error by \(2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\).  Conditional on the corresponding cross-fit training sigma-field, the independent replacement of block \(k\) has range at most \(L_k\).  Applying (1) to the two parity sums, adding the deterministic discarded-index bound \(L_{\mathcal G}\) and the treated-mean bound \(r_B\), and using the defining scalar optimization for \(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\), gives
\[
 \Pr\{\text{calendar stochastic error}>r_{\mathrm{cal}}\mid z_0\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2.
\tag{3}
\]
Because \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\), the event that the stochastic error exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}\) is contained in the union of the events in (2)--(3).  Its probability is at most \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\).

Spectral clipping gives \(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I\).  Projection is nonexpansive, balanced folds have \(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and donor unbiasedness and ellipticity give
\[
 \mathbb E\{N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\mid z_0\}
 \le\frac{6SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{4}
\]
Markov's inequality and a union bound over at most two folds, with the stated \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\), imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell
 \|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mid z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{5}
\]
On the complement of (5), \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I\), Holder continuity, local-constant bias, and selected-certificate optimality bound the deterministic error by \(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Equations (2)--(5) and \(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) prove coverage on the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch the interval is \([-2B,2B]\).  Bounded wealth and the identification lemma put \(\tau(z_0)\) in this range, so coverage there is one.

We next bound length.  Since \(r=0\), every regular fitted response weight is nonnegative and \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\).  Hence
\[
 r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C_\alpha A^{1/2},
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le r_{\mathrm{unit}}.
\tag{6}
\]
On the event where the comparison pair \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is admissible, selected-certificate optimality and the bandwidth floor give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen yield \(\mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Taking expectations in (7) and applying \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
All deterministic small-sample branches disappear eventually along the stated growth arrays.  The remaining geometry-failure contribution is at most \(4B\Pr(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}\).  Equations (4) and (6)--(8) of \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} then prove the expected-length upper bound.  Calendar independence replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under each law implies
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1),
\]
and therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose the treated-sign displacement in (8)--(9) of the conditional proof small enough that its Hellinger common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); (9) gives \(c_\alpha A^{1/2}\).  Under \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), the donor construction in \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} has a freely chosen standardized displacement multiplier.  Taking it small makes its common mass exceed \(2\alpha\) while retaining separation \(c_\alpha N^{-\lambda/2}\); (9) gives the donor lower bound.  Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} gives common mass greater than \(2\alpha\) and separation \(c_\alpha\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  The independent-calendar no-hit construction gives its \(T^{-\lambda/d}\) counterpart.  Taking the largest channel and using the smoothing domination (4) proves the expected-length lower bound.

Let \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  We first construct a regular donor location family satisfying the full covariance and fourth-moment restrictions.  Choose \(a_D>1\) so that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) sufficiently small, put a variable \(V_u\) on \(\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) with probabilities
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
At \(u=0\) all three probabilities are strictly positive, so they remain positive on a fixed neighborhood of zero.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E V_u=u,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Let the remaining \(q-1\) standardized donor coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.  At \(u=0\), independence and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =q(q-1)+(q-1)+a_D^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.
\tag{4}
\]
The left side with centering at the mean \(u\) is a continuous polynomial in \(u\) and the probabilities (2); consequently it remains below \(B^4\) for all sufficiently small \(|u|\).

Set \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and \(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where \(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Because \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths obey the interior restriction for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under law \(v\in\{0,1\}\), take the first donor coordinate to be \(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\), take the other coordinates to be \(1/2\) plus the common Rademacher coordinates, and make donors i.i.d.  Equations (3)--(4) show that
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (5) verifies full covariance ellipticity.

All three baseline probabilities in (2) are positive and differentiable in \(u\).  The mean-value theorem applied to their square roots therefore gives a constant \(C_0\), depending only on the fixed moment slack, such that the one-donor squared Hellinger distance is at most \(C_0\delta_N^2\).  Hellinger affinity multiplies under products.  Moreover, if \(p,q\) are densities and \(A=\int\sqrt{pq}\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \frac12\int|p-q|
 \le\frac12\{(2-2A)(2+2A)\}^{1/2}
 =(1-A^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Choosing the fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most \(1-\eta_0\) for some \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common independent uniform training design.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), set \(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set the other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  Choosing fixed positive \(b_0,b_1\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,L\) puts every surface in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), keeps its values strictly inside \([-B,B]\), and gives
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.
\tag{7}
\]
Take identical bounded centered response noise in the two laws, so that \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})+\varepsilon_{sti}\), and take identical positive constant treated observations.  Set \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and choose the unobserved \(B_{si}(0)\) to be the positive constant \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  With amplitudes small enough, all wealth levels lie in \((0,B)\).  To realize them as buy-and-hold levels in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, set \(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\).  The defining product then equals \(B_{si}(a)\).  Independence makes the calendar sequence i.i.d., gives cross-unit independence and donor--training separation, and verifies both design-conditional centering equalities.  Consistency and event-date transport hold by construction.

The complete training and treated-event observed laws are identical under the two alternatives.  By \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7), their targets differ by
\[
 \pi_1b_1\delta_N^\kappa
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) proves the claim without any lower local-modulus restriction.

Let \(q=Sd\).  The condition \(B^4\ge q^2\) permits a common donor law \(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), where the coordinates of \(U_j\) are independent Rademacher variables.  It has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and standardized fourth moment \(q^2\); it is independent of all panel variables below.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and set
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.
\tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by \(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) of volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw all design points in block \(b\) independently uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on its complement.  Thus at every complete-block time the marginal density is exactly
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Draw the incomplete block and the other cohorts independently and uniformly.

If \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) indices can share at most one block label.  Replacing that label by an independent copy fails with probability at most \(2p_T\), so \(\beta(k)\le2p_T\); if \(k\ge L_T\), the relevant labels are disjoint and \(\beta(k)=0\).  Equation (2) therefore gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1).
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete block has label zero and that no point of the incomplete block falls in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  Since the incomplete block has fewer than \(L_T\) observations, its extra failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), while
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}=:\eta_\alpha>2\alpha.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of that smaller cube and take a fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported on the unit ball, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  For a sufficiently small fixed \(a>0\), define
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+a h_T^\lambda
 \phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),
\tag{6}
\]
and keep all other cohort surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  Holder scaling makes the \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) norm of the added bump bounded uniformly in \(T\); choosing \(a,b_0\) small enforces both the Holder radius and bounded wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces in other cohorts, keep positive treated observations identical, impose consistency, and set the unobserved untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Choose all amplitudes so these levels lie in \((0,B)\), and realize each as in \texttt{def:buyhold-level} by taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and all later returns zero.  Then design-conditional centering and event-date transport are exact, cross-unit independence holds, and the joint design--response sequence inherits (4).  On \(E_T\), every observed response lies outside the bump support, so the restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide.  They consequently possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1a h_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{7}
\]
This proves the certificate over the base Holder class.

Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the integer-order convention gives \(r=0\), and the local-polynomial Gram matrix is scalar.  \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \le C R_\star^{1/2}.
\]
These conclusions use no lower local-modulus condition, count the full-range interval on every declared bad-sample branch, and never divide by an estimated variance.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), every random interval \(I_\alpha\) with the same uniform conditional coverage obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c R_\star^{1/2}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.  On the independent-calendar subclass, both upper and lower spacing terms are \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The theorem makes no higher-order claim for \(\lambda>1\).

There are constants \(c_0>0\) and \(\eta_0>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws whose realized interior paths are separated by order \(N^{-1/2}\), whose observed-data total variation distance is at most \(1-\eta_0\), and whose causal targets are separated by at least \(c_0N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and treated-event observed laws can be chosen identical; only the donor-location experiment and the transported untreated potential mean differ.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.

Suppose \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0\le1/2\).  For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) there are constants \(c_\alpha>0\) and \(\eta_\alpha>2\alpha\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws with the same interior realized path whose observed-data laws possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\), while their causal targets differ by at least
\[
 c_\alpha\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
Both laws satisfy the frozen geometric beta-mixing envelope and the design-conditional centering assumption.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.

For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the separately defined deterministic fixed-design experiment has minimax MSE at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) for all fixed designs and has minimax MSE \(\asymp R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) when \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\); every causal law inherits the conditional upper bound for almost every realized design.  The anchor estimator has the computable upper certificate \(R_D\). prose_updates.tldr: The causal target remains cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a realized event path, identified only by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality.  The base model now contains the Holder, centering, mixing, boundedness, and donor-moment conditions but no class-wide lower local modulus.  Fixed-design difficulty is stated in a deterministic induced product experiment for every exact design, eliminating arbitrary regular-conditional versions at null designs; causal laws inherit its upper bound almost surely in the realized design.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nearest-design and anchor estimators attain the conditional and marginal upper rates, while explicit distance, rare-cluster, treated-mean, and regular donor witnesses give matching lower rates.  The nonredundant marginal channels are treated replication, calendar spacing, and donor location; geometric beta mixing incurs \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\), whereas i.i.d. calendars give \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  The donor converse correctly requires strict fourth-moment and interior slack; exact constants and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an externally generated query, while a conditional minimax statement at every continuously distributed design is ill posed if it ranges over arbitrary versions of regular conditional laws.  The substantive fixed-design object is the deterministic product-experiment modulus, not Gram invertibility or a class-wide lower direction.
project_justification.niche: Historical market paths may be recorded exactly even when the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  This separates realized-site optimal recovery, full-covariance donor-location uncertainty, and the untestable causal transport equality.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the causal observed-law functional, defines a deterministic fixed-design product experiment and its joint modulus, and proves a rough-Holder frontier using explicit treated-mean, distance-function, donor-location, and rare-cluster witnesses.  The lower constructions lie directly in the base Holder class and need no attainable-local-modulus assumption.  The anchor/extrapolation rule remains a computable upper certificate and attains the corrected marginal and honest-length rates.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event paths have density bounded above and away from zero.  Conditional analysis is an ordinary minimax problem in the separately defined deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for every fixed \(X\); causal conditional kernels enter it for almost every realized design.  The Gram radius certifies an estimator but is never a minimax converse.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per calendar window and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes.  Given the exact design and realized path, untreated responses are centered at \(m_s(X_{st})\), treated outcomes retain their path-conditional mean, and histories are independent across units.  Dependence within one unit's training and event history remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; neither design-conditional centering nor any local modulus identifies this causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary.  Exact fixed-design recovery can be easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the realized path.  A nondegenerate donor-location converse requires \(\delta_0<1/2\); at the endpoint the admissible path set can collapse to the cube center.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event path is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence.  The upper bounds need only ellipticity and the fourth-moment envelope.  The donor lower experiment uses the necessary strict slack \(B^4>(Sd)^2\); at equality the scalar donor class can collapse to singular symmetric two-point laws.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) supplies the classical Gaussian link between a linear-functional modulus and near-minimax affine estimation; the present result derives a bounded-response, rough-Holder product-experiment comparison with a generated full-covariance query.  Stone (1982) and Fan (1993) give ordinary Holder and pointwise local-polynomial benchmarks but not replicated sites plus a generated center.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) perturb every training coordinate, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study classical error in every latent coordinate; neither experiment applies to an exact historical design with only the event center generated.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study sample-split evaluation at an estimated minimizer, where strong convexity changes the location channel.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware interval calculations, and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) motivate dependent block calibration.  These sources inform the architecture; the deterministic induced experiment, nearest-site characterization, donor-product combination, and three-channel panel frontier are derived here.
prose_updates.interpretation: Conditionally, two exact designs with the same Gram certificate can have different difficulty: an exact site at the event path eliminates spatial recovery error, whereas a nearby hole leaves a Holder-sized ambiguity.  This statement is made in a deterministic experiment for each design, while the causal transfer is asserted only for almost every realized design.  Marginally, occupancy converts the ambiguity into the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing, provided the donor class contains a regular overlapping location subfamily; no regression lower-modulus assumption is involved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion relies on exact historical paths.  The constructive frontier is proved for \(0<\lambda\le1\), where nearest-site and local-constant weights are nonnegative and have unit absolute mass.  For \(\lambda>1\), controlling the conditional stochastic norm of signed higher-order recovery weights remains open.  Geometric beta mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty, with a no-log i.i.d. corollary.  The donor lower bound requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\); without this slack the allowed donor experiment can be singular and the root-\(N\) location lower bound need not hold.  Exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction.  Design-conditional centering is a distinct observed-law sampling condition.  All upper-risk, coverage, and expected-length results for \(0<\lambda\le1\) hold on the base Holder class without \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}.  The spacing and fixed-design recovery converses also need no such modulus.  The donor-location contribution to the MSE and honest-length converses requires the disclosed, necessary nondegeneracy \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\).  Growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-path bands, exact constants, and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
The parameter restrictions in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} give \(a_0>0\).  The displayed matrix \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, as is also verified below, so \(q_0>0\).  We first verify membership in the base Holder panel class obtained from \texttt{def:panel-model-class} after removing \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}; we then prove the modulus assertion separately.  The latter calculation also verifies the additional attainable-modulus condition in the unrepaired displayed version of the class.

At the event path \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), both formulas for \(m_1\) give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and \(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Hence the construction and the support \(\eta_{si}\in\{-1,1\}\) imply
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad B_{si}(1)=B_{si}(0)+a_0\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular, \(B_{si}(a)>0\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), so \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\).  Since \(W_{si,-1}=1\) and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\), the definition of buy-and-hold wealth gives
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equals one when \(H=0\).  The prescribed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) is exactly \texttt{ass:consistency}.  Independence and centering of \(\eta_{si}\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.  Each potential wealth path uses only the corresponding unit's noise and the contemporaneous path label, so this construction has no anticipation and no spillovers.

We next check boundedness and smoothness.  In the case \(\kappa=1\), put \(y=x_1-1/2\).  For \(y\in[-1/2,1/2]\), one has \(-1/4\le y+y^2\le3/4\), and therefore
\[
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive and negative parts in the displayed definition of \(m_1\) cannot both be nonzero, whence
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
For \(s>1\), \(m_s(x)=4a_0\).  Since \(\varepsilon_{sti},\eta_{si}\in\{-1,1\}\), these bounds and the two event-outcome values above give
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le 6a_0
 \le \frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds.

When \(0<\lambda<1\), one has \(\kappa=\lambda\).  The elementary inequality
\[
 |v_+^{\lambda}-w_+^{\lambda}|\le |v-w|^{\lambda}
\]
and the analogous inequality for negative parts show, separately on each side of zero, that the \(\lambda\)-Holder seminorm of the nonconstant part of \(m_1\) is at most \(a_0\).  If the arguments lie on opposite sides of zero, their signed coordinate distances add, so the triangle inequality gives the bound \(3a_0/2\).  Consequently the standard isotropic Holder norm is bounded by
\[
 \|m_1\|_{\infty}+[m_1]_{\lambda}
 \le 5a_0+\frac{3a_0}{2}<7a_0<L.
\]
When \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is the quadratic surface and its only possibly nonzero derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant \(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); and all derivatives of order greater than two vanish.  With the stated order reduction at integer \(\lambda\), the usual isotropic Holder norm is therefore at most \(9a_0<L\) for every \(\lambda\ge1\).  Each constant surface has norm \(4a_0<L\).  This proves \texttt{ass:holder-regression} for every cohort.  The selected surface is non-affine: it has a nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\) and a non-affine asymmetric cusp when \(0<\kappa<1\).

The paths \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  The declared ranges \(c_X\le1\le C_X\) verify \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  Because the path draws and all response noises are independent across calendar periods, each cohort's joint calendar sequence is independent.  Its absolute-regularity coefficients therefore satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1),
\]
as required by \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\).  Independence and centering of the response noises imply, for every \(s,t,i\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st})+a_0\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st}),
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are precisely the two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), the arrays \((\varepsilon_{sti},\eta_{si})\) are mutually independent across \((s,i)\), proving \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The \(X_{st}\) are observed directly, which is \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.  Product-law independence of the donor Rademacher vectors from \(\mathcal X\), the response noises, and the event noises proves \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  The construction is nondegenerate because
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0)=a_0^2>0.
\]

It remains to check the donor law.  The vectors \(U_j\) are independent and identically distributed with \(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  Thus
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}.  For
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12I_{Sd}+\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top},
\]
the vector \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) has eigenvalue one, and every vector orthogonal to it has eigenvalue one half.  Therefore the restrictions \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge1\) imply
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
\]
which is \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  In particular, \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, and each off-diagonal entry equals \(1/(2Sd)>0\).  Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  All conditions of the repaired base version of \texttt{def:panel-model-class} have now been verified, so \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) after the directed removal of the attainable-modulus premise.

We now prove the separate local-modulus assertion.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), define
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Since \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\), direct calculation gives
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta
 =\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} also yields
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le \delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Because \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), it follows that \(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.

Only the first coordinate of the first cohort contributes to the weighted increment.  If \(\kappa=1\), then the stacked weighted gradient at \(z_0\) is \(\pi_1a_0\bar e\) and has strictly positive covariance-standardized norm
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Substitution of \(u_\delta\) gives the exact increment
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
In particular, it is at least \(\pi_1a_0q_0\delta\).  If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) instead gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
These displays prove a lower bound \(c_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa\), where
\[
 c_{\mathrm{ex}}=\pi_1a_0\min\{q_0,q_0^\kappa\}>0.
\]
Under the optional restriction \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le c_{\mathrm{ex}}\) displayed in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp}, they also verify \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus} for the unrepaired class.

For the reverse inequality, take any perturbation \(u\) feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.  The upper ellipticity bound gives
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Write \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) implies \(|v|\le1/2\).  When \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), the two branches of the asymmetric cusp give
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Every other cohort surface is constant and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the supremum over feasible \(u\) proves \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa\) for a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{ex}}\).  Together with the preceding lower bound,
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
Thus the bounded noisy law is a nondegenerate member of the repaired base Holder class and, as a logically separate property of this particular law, has the asserted attainable covariance-standardized modulus.  No lower modulus for an arbitrary member of the base class has been inferred.

Let
\[
 \mathcal X=\sigma\!\left((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T}\right),
 \qquad
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Because \(E\in\mathcal X\), the random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is bounded and measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The assumed representation \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\), together with the defining property of conditional expectation, therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely under the conditional law given }z_0.
\tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking the conditional expectation given \(z_0\) in the shock representation yields
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=bp_E.
\]
Combining this identity with (1)--(2) shows that \(b\mathbf 1_E=bp_E\) almost surely under the conditional law given \(z_0\).  Hence
\[
 0
 =\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2p_E(1-p_E).
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (3) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Because \(p_E\in[0,1]\), it follows that \(p_E\in\{0,1\}\).

For the stated former scalar construction, \(z_0\) is fixed, \(X_{11}\) is uniform on \([0,1]\), and \(q\in(0,1)\).  Therefore
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)
 =\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)
 =q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (3).  Thus its shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, that law is not in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Since the former obstruction required both members of its two-law experiment to lie in the model class, that experiment is excluded.  No causal transport condition is used in this argument.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), and a unit \(i\), and define
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
The conditional mean exists by \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}.  By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(W\) be bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable.  Then \(W\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\), and the pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation applied to (4) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
Now let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and write \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\).  Substitution of \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) into (5) yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=\mu_{si}p_E.
\]
When \(p_E>0\), the definition of conditioning on an event and division by \(p_E\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.
\tag{6}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E^c]=\mu_{si}
\tag{7}
\]
whenever \(p_E<1\).  Thus (6)--(7) apply simultaneously when \(0<p_E<1\).  The exclusion of the former common-design-shock experiment is exactly \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

It remains to show directly that conditional centering does not fix the centered event-noise constant.  We construct two laws for every positive \(N,T,n_1\).  Choose the admissible scalar fixed parameters
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\]
take \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), and fix any \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  Define the untreated regression and training experiment by
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12
 \quad(1\le t\le T,\ 1\le i\le n_1).
\tag{8}
\]
Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the training experiment, and set
\[
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j,
 \qquad 1\le j\le N.
\tag{9}
\]
For every event unit, put \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
\tag{10}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), put \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), let \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_{n_1}\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the design and donor variables, and put \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In both laws impose \texttt{ass:consistency} by defining \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold formula then yields
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }P^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.
\tag{11}
\]
All constructed returns lie in \((-1,\infty)\), since their smallest value is \(-1/2\).

We verify membership in the base model class condition by condition.  Equations (8), (10), and (11) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The constant function \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\) and Holder seminorm zero, and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), as required by \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_X(x)=1\quad(0\le x\le1),
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density}.

Conditional on the complete design array, all training outcomes in (8) are deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\), the event outcomes are also deterministic; under \(P^{(1)}\), the event outcome of unit \(i\) is a function only of \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence of the \(\varepsilon_i\)'s therefore proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The calendar blocks in (8) are independent over \(t\), so their beta-mixing coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Declaring the \(X_{1t}\)'s in (8) to be directly observed verifies \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Equation (8) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(X_{1t}).
\tag{12}
\]
Under either law, (11), independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\tag{13}
\]
Thus both equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} hold.

By (9), conditional on the fixed \(z_0=1/2\), the donor scores are independent and identically distributed, are independent of the training and event samples, and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0)=1.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Since \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), equation (14) also proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}; and
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[|\xi_j|^4]
 =1
 =B^4,
\tag{15}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} while retaining the full scalar covariance.

Finally, (8) and (10) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(z_0),
\tag{16}
\]
so \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} holds.  Consistency was imposed before (11).  We have therefore verified every member property in the directed base-class post-image of \texttt{def:panel-model-class}.  In particular, the construction uses no directional lower-modulus premise.

The joint law of the arrays \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) is the same under \(P^{(0)}\) and \(P^{(1)}\) by (8)--(9).  By \texttt{def:target}, (10)--(11), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(0)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0,\\
 \tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(1)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac14\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Nevertheless, (11) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus the centering restriction permits both event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  Equations (4)--(7) prove the asserted orthogonality and eventwise mean invariance, and (8)--(18) prove the explicit two-law certificate.  Removing the invalid common-shock witness is therefore logically distinct from calculating any sharp minimax constant for the remaining centered product experiment.

proposed.statement:
Every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) satisfies the conditional orthogonality
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)\right\}W\mid z_0\right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence every design event \(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)<1\) has the same conditional treated mean on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} removes the former common-design-shock obstruction.  This repair does not by itself determine an exact asymptotic minimax constant: there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\) having the same joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered product experiment.
proposed.justification: The theorem records exactly what the repaired sampling model rules out and why that repair is not an exact-constant calculation.
proposed.gap: Exact constants for the remaining centered optimal-recovery product experiment are left to the fresh open question.
proposed.consumer: The model-class audit can remove the obsolete negative answer without overstating what centering proves.
